content_voiceover: D U X four rearranged ALL has a distinctive and somewhat paradoxical M R D pattern that's worth knowing cold for boards. Early on, at days eight and fifteen, these patients tend to show poor M R D clearance, and the proposed explanation is relative resistance to asparaginase during that early phase of therapy. But by day forty-two, the picture flips, and D U X four rearranged ALL shows excellent M R D clearance, likely because these leukemic cells are actually quite sensitive to six-mercaptopurine, ara-C, and cyclophosphamide, the drugs that come later in consolidation. The bar chart on the right compares the proportion of M R D-positive cases across timepoints for E T V six colon colon R U N X one, hyperdiploidy greater than fifty, and D U X four rearranged, and you can see the D U X four bars behave differently from the other favorable subtypes, starting high and dropping sharply. The key takeaway is, don't panic and don't escalate therapy just because a D U X four rearranged patient has sluggish early M R D, because by day forty-two, the disease usually clears nicely, and overall this subtype carries a favorable prognosis.
